t:
Amounts made available under the “Medical Services”, “Medical Community Care”, “Medical Support and Compliance”, “Medical Facilities”, “General Operating Expenses, Veterans Benefits Administration”, “Board of Veterans Appeals”, “General Administration”, and “National Cemetery Administration” accounts for fiscal year 2020 may be transferred to or from the “Information Technology Systems” account:  Provided, That such transfers may not result in a more than 10 percent aggregate increase in the 
total amount made available by this Act for the “Information Technology Systems” account:  Provided further, That, before a transfer may take place, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall request from the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress the authority to make the transfer and an approval is issued.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that requiring a request and approval before a transfer is a consultation step before a federal decision. But the only parties involved are the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and the congressional Appropriations Committees, all of which are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public takes part, so this is intra-government coordination and not participation.
fable.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall request from the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress the authority to make the transfer and an approval is issued

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to obtain approval from Congressional Appropriations Committees before making a budget transfer. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government (inside the boundary). Therefore, this interaction is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_block.s: before a transfer may take place, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall request from the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress the authority to make the transfer and an approval is issued.

opus.w: This section only lets the VA move money between appropriations accounts. The one procedural step is getting approval from the congressional Appropriations Committees, which are inside the federal government. It may look like participation because a federal decision depends on someone else's approval, but no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, so it does not meet the definition.
opus.s: before a transfer may take place, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall request from the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress the authority to make the transfer and an approval is issued
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is participation, because the Secretary has to ask for and get approval before transferring funds. That fails because the approval comes from the House and Senate Appropriations Committees, which are part of Congress and so inside the federal government. No outside party is involved.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to obtain approval from the Committees on Appropriations of Congress before making certain fund transfers. Since Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, this interaction is intra-governmental coordination. The definition explicitly states that reports to or notifications of Congress are not participation.
qwen_chat.s: before a transfer may take place, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall request from the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress the authority to make the transfer and an approval is issued.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary must request authority from Congress, this involves an outside party. However, Congress is explicitly defined as being INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, coordination with Congress is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation under the definition.
